gen-righteous-fs-asap: Asap keeps things readable, with open arcs for its c forms and a lowercase nearly as tall as the capitals. Asap's sans steps back while Righteous, bent like thin steel rod, holds one unbroken line weight throughout.
gen-righteous-fs-epilogue: Epilogue has curvy, unclamped letters, a tall-bodied lowercase and stubby ascender tips. Epilogue's wire-like monoline skeleton lets Righteous, with bowls filling the line, take the loud spot at the top.
gen-righteous-fs-fira-sans: Righteous bends bold, steel-rod letters with bowls that fill the line. Righteous is best at making an entrance, while Fira Sans, with s curves open at both ends and a large x-height, is best at being read.
gen-righteous-fs-merriweather-sans: A single squeezed-toothpaste line forms every Righteous letter. Merriweather Sans, a sans-serif with sturdy tall lowercase, plus an e that opens clearly to the right, gives that bold stroke something steady to stand beside.
gen-gf-paprika-montserrat: Montserrat glides under the eye with oversized e and a counters and plenty of white space leading into each curve. Paprika scatters its big letters; let Montserrat stay modest in size.
gen-gf-revalia-general-sans: Revalia strides across widely separated letters, bold and expressive, with a g whose lower curve stays open. General Sans holds a steady pen pressure from first letter to last, its bent-paperclip strokes never swelling.
gen-gf-snowburst-one-switzer: Switzer reads like bent wire, tubular letters with c tips that never creep toward touching and a tall waist line. Snowburst One does the stencil showing off; Switzer does the reading.
gen-gf-tektur-work-sans: Expressive, with outsized lowercase proportions, Tektur gives its curves generous openings and a pipe-cleaner look. But Work Sans, a modern sans-serif whose c tips stay apart, carries paragraph after paragraph without fuss.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-satoshi: Tube-like and loud, that is Tilt Neon, with a splayed c terminal. Satoshi, a sans-serif with a soaring x-height and an e that never looks squeezed shut, gives it a friendly, steady partner.
gen-dafont-starborn-fs-supreme: Supreme is crisp, with a thick, heavy-looking strip of text and letters held open, never curled shut. And paragraphs of it would read steadily, while Starborn floats above in dreamy blank space.
